images.title: Three views of a cone
images.purpose: Show the front, top and side views of one standing cone.
images.composition: One cone in the centre with its three views placed around it, each named in one word.
images.exact_structure: Centre: one cone standing on its base, filled teal #0072B2 with thin dark outline. Above it, the top view: a circle with a dot at its centre, amber #E69F00 outline, labelled 'top'. To its left, the front view: an isosceles triangle as wide as the circle, amber outline, labelled 'front'. To its right, the side view: the same isosceles triangle, amber outline, labelled 'side'. Each view joined to the cone by one thin grey #6B7280 arrow pointing from the view towards the cone, so each view sits where the eye looks from. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A standing cone looks like a triangle from the front and side and a circle from the top.
images.description: Show the front, top and side views of one standing cone.
images.context: One clean concept image for T11.C3.

image_decisions.why: The practice tool turns a solid to read its views; one solid with its three views shows the move.
